key_insight: An LLM can be trained with solver feedback to generate MILP instances that are not just feasible, but intentionally hard for branch-and-bound solvers.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical way to create stronger optimization benchmarks and stress-test solvers without requiring seed instances or manual parameter tuning.
method: Use a challenger-solver self-play setup where the LLM proposes instances and the solver scores feasibility plus hardness.
Define rewards from solver signals such as branch-and-bound node counts and post-cut relaxation gaps.
Fine-tune Gemma-4-12B and Qwen3.5-4B with GRPO and a size curriculum to produce OptiScribe models.
evidence_signal: On capacitated facility location and max-cut, the trained models increased median SCIP nodes by 1.7-5x for OptiScribe-12B and up to 15.6x for OptiScribe-4B, while also improving feasibility and post-cut gaps.
watch_item: The approach depends on solver-specific feedback, so generalization across solvers, formulations, and instance families may require careful retuning.
paper_title: Teaching LLMs to Generate Challenging MILP Instances via Solver Feedback
